metadata.case_name: SHABBINA KHOKHAR v. EUROPE BEAUTY INTERNATIONAL LTD

source: As a result of the treatment received from the Defendant, the Plaintiff suffered multiple burn wounds over her arms.
She was diagnosed to have suffered burns to both of her arms.

Dr. Ma observed multiple bullae and erythematous patches over her arms with great pain and exudates. He diagnosed the Plaintiff to have suffered 2nd to 3rd degree of burn on both arms and recommended daily dressing and treatment.
Dr. Ho noted multiple burn wound over the Plaintiff’s upper limbs, with 80% being 1st degree burns and 20% being 2nd degree burns.
Dr. Nicholson opined that the scars are consistent with burn injury from ultra-pulsed light therapy and the Plaintiff has suffered from permanent cosmetic disability.

manifestations.description: painful burning sensation on her arms at the locations treated
red, swollen and painful wounds on the arms
multiple bullae and erythematous patches over her arms with great pain and exudates
pain when pulling off the old bandages during redressing as the bandages would stick to the burn wounds
wounds took over a month to heal and she was unable to move her arms because of pain and the bandages
could not shower, wash her hair, change her clothes by herself, eat certain food, drive, or even type during recovery
post-inflammatory hypopigmentation which may last for 6 to 12 months

noticeable area of hyperpigmentation on the posterior aspect of the right shoulder with no hair present; conspicuous areas of irregularly pigmented scar on the right arm near the elbow region and hypopigmented pale scars (sizes described); areas of irregular hypopigmented scar near the elbow region of the left arm; mild scattered pigment changes
unwanted dark hair on the Plaintiff’s arms (evidence that the Defendant’s IPL treatment has had no effect)
mild hypersensitivity in the region of the right elbow scar

treatments_received: Accident and Emergency Department attendance at Prince of Wales Hospital on 21st November 2005; wounds dressed and treated with cream to prevent infection
Follow-up treatment by family doctor Dr. Ma with daily dressing and treatment
Plastic surgery assessment by Dr. Ian Nicholson

losses.description: Permanent cosmetic disability with pigment irregularity and hypopigmented scars on both arms, including conspicuous irregularly pigmented scars and hypopigmented pale scars as described by Dr. Nicholson.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Prior to the injury the Plaintiff was active in hiking, swimming and playing badminton. She no longer feels comfortable taking part in activities that expose her arms.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: The Plaintiff feels she has to hide her arms at all times and she no longer feels comfortable wearing clothing that exposes her arms, causing embarrassment and anxiety especially around her wedding.
